AS2026-0009.highlights: Australia’s sugar production is forecast to increase by nine percent to 4.18 million metric tons (MMT) in marketing year (MY) 2026/27, from an estimated 3.83 MMT in MY 2025/26. Sugar cane production is projected to reach 30.7 MMT, an eight percent increase year-on-year, supported by both improved yields and a modest expansion in harvested area. The production increase reflects a return to a full growing cycle in MY 2026/27, following a shortened MY 2025/26 season caused by the late completion of the preceding harvest. Favorable seasonal conditions have supported a normal planting program and are expected to improve cane yields and sugar content. Raw sugar exports are forecast to rise significantly to 3.6 MMT in MY 2026/27, compared to an estimated 2.7 MMT in the previous year. Refined sugar exports are expected to remain stable at approximately 10,000 metric tons (MT). Domestic consumption, typically accounting for around 20 percent of production, is forecast to increase modestly due to population growth.
AS2026-0009.name: Sugar Annual

The reduction reflects very dry conditions across much of the cane-growing region from April 2026, after broadly favorable conditions earlier in the growing season. Despite the smaller cane crop, high sugar content in cane harvested to date is expected to lift sugar production by 4.4 percent to 4.0 MMT from 3.83 MMT in the prior year. Raw sugar exports are estimated at 3.5 MMT, up 34 percent from 2.62 MMT in MY 2025/26, supported by higher sugar production, elevated carry-in stocks, and improved world sugar prices.

BR2026-0008.file: Brewing Opportunity - Brazil's Specialty Coffee Sector Shows Strong Potential_Brasilia_Brazil_BR2026-0008
BR2026-0008.highlights: Brazil, the world’s largest coffee producer and exporter, has recently experienced a rise in domestic appreciation and production of specialty coffee. This growth is driven by dedicated producers, and strong research networks. Production, often small-scale and linked to sustainability certifications, requires significant investment and expertise, with profitability limited by challenges such as restricted access to credit, postharvest infrastructure, and technical support. The United States is the main export market, and Brazil is actively promoting specialty coffee globally through initiatives focused on quality and innovation.
BR2026-0008.name: Brewing Opportunity - Brazil's Specialty Coffee Sector Shows Strong Potential

Despite this, yields remain stable and Brazil is set to maintain its position as the world’s leading cotton exporter, supported by strong international demand. Domestic consumption is forecast to remain steady, while ending stocks are projected to decline due to lower production.
BR2026-0019.name: Cotton and Products Annual

BR2026-0020.highlights: Brazil remains the world's largest sugarcane and sugar producer. Despite higher sugarcane production forecast for MY2026/27, the harvest is expected to favor ethanol over sugar production, reducing sugar output and exports. This shift is directly linked to domestic gasoline prices, since higher gasoline prices make ethanol more profitable relative to sugar, changing the production mix accordingly. Brazil is the second-largest recipient of the U.S. sugar tariff-rate quota, representing approximately 14 percent of the total TRQ, and has consistently met its allocation in recent years. On January 17, 2026, the EU and Mercosur signed an agreement granting Mercosur exporters duty-free access for 180,000 metric tons of raw cane sugar for refining. The EU-Mercosur quotas to be assigned to Brazil will be allocated exclusively to North-Northeastern sugar producers, consistent with the allocation methodology for U.S. sugar TRQs and in accordance with specific federal legislation.
BR2026-0020.name: Sugar Annual

BR2026-0036.highlights: Brazil’s cotton outlook for MY 2026/27 indicates a slight reduction of harvested area due to high production costs, price volatility, and weather related production delays. Record productivity is expected to partially offset this area contraction, resulting in only a minor production decline. Strong export performance characterized the end of the MY 2025/26 trade season, driven mainly by robust demand from Asian markets. Domestic consumption and exports in MY 2026/27 are both forecast to remain stable, supported by a favorable exchange rate and cotton’s recent competitiveness boost against synthetic fibers. Meanwhile, ending stocks are expected to decline as a result of a tighter supply balance, which could provide further upward support for cotton prices.

BR2026-0039.highlights: Irregular rainfall linked to El Niño is already affecting the crushing pace in Brazil's Center-South (CS), the country's main sugarcane-producing region. A few mills are expected to keep crushing into the off-season, but the region will still likely carry cane over into MY 2027/28 (known in Brazil as cana bisada). In the North and Northeast (NNE), the MY 2026/27 harvest began in September, and production should stay close to the historical average despite El Niño. Weaker foreign demand for sugar and lower world prices have led producers to shift their production mix toward ethanol, which lowers sugar export estimates. For FY 2027, the United States reduced Brazil's raw sugar tariff-rate quota (TRQ) allocation to 100,000 metric tons, raw value (MTRV), about 55,000 MTRV less than in previous years.

BR2026-0040.file: Bracing for Impact - How the 2026 El Nino Affects Brazil's Agriculture_Brasilia_Brazil_BR2026-0040
BR2026-0040.highlights: The arrival of the 2026/27 El Niño brings renewed uncertainty to Brazil's agricultural sector, with regional impacts varying widely. Central and Northern areas face higher risks of heatwaves and below-average rainfall, while the South is bracing for excessive precipitation. These shifts threaten to disrupt planting schedules for soybeans and second-season corn, reduce water availability for pastures, and strain livestock welfare. High temperatures may also jeopardize critical coffee and orange flowering periods as well as sugarcane yields. In response, Brazilian producers should be prepared for elevated input costs, rising insurance premiums, and recurring infrastructure vulnerabilities associated with severe weather events. These financial impacts may have lasting effects well into future harvests, heightening the strain on Brazil’s agricultural sector.
BR2026-0040.name: Bracing for Impact - How the 2026 El Nino Affects Brazil's Agriculture

BR2026-0049.highlights: Post lowers its MY 2026/27 sugarcane production forecast to 681 million metric tons (MMT), down 2 percent from the previous estimate. Above-average rainfall in the Center-South in September and October slowed crushing and lowered total recoverable sugar (TRS) levels. Because sugarcane quality is lower, Post also cuts its sugar production forecast by 4 percent to 40.5 MMT and its sugar export forecast by 4.8 percent to 31.7 MMT. Post keeps the sugar-ethanol mix at 49 percent sugar and 51 percent ethanol. Analysts expect about 30 MMT of sugarcane to carry over into MY 2027/28.
BR2026-0049.name: Sugar November Update

CO2026-0008.highlights: In Marketing Year (MY) 2026/2027, Colombian coffee production is forecast to increase 7.2 percent to 13.4 million bags green bean equivalent (GBE), mainly due to favorable dry conditions. This increase follows a transition from La Niña to a strong El Niño. Coffee plants can withstand water stress and elevated temperatures, especially when cultivated in soils with good moisture retention that prevent critical water deficit. Decreasing coffee prices are encouraging replanting and renovations. As a result of higher production, Colombian coffee exports are expected to increase to 13.4 million bags in MY 2026/2027. The United States remains the top export destination for Colombian coffee, followed by the European Union and Japan.
CO2026-0008.name: Coffee Annual

CO2026-0036.highlights: In Marketing Year (MY) 2026/2027, Colombian coffee production is forecast to increase 5.9 percent to 13.4 million bags green bean equivalent (GBE) as growing conditions normalize after the excessive La Niña rains that reduced the MY 2025/2026 crop. This increase follows a transition from La Niña to a strong El Niño. However, El Niño is expected to bring well-below-normal rainfall through early 2027, a downside risk to flowering for the 2027 harvest. Decreasing coffee prices are encouraging replanting and renovations. Post forecasts MY 2026/2027 exports at 12.6 million bags and imports at 1.4 million bags. For MY 2025/2026, Post revises production up to 12.65 million bags GBE, and revises exports down to 12.1 million bags and imports down to 1.7 million bags.. The United States remains the top export destination for Colombian coffee, followed by the European Union, Canada, and Japan.

E42026-0032.highlights: EU sugar production in MY 2026/27 is forecast to decline further, as persistently low prices reduce beet sowing across major producing Member States. Exports are expected to fall in line with lower output, while imports are projected to increase. Consumption remains broadly stable, although a gradual structural decline continues, driven by demographic trends, health awareness, and industry reformulation. The Inward Processing regime, which allows duty-free imports of sugar for processing in the EU when the resulting products are re-exported, has emerged as a key market concern, with significant inflows prompting a temporary suspension by the European Commission. Trade policy developments continue to weigh on sentiment, with the European Commission advancing multiple free trade agreements, including Mercosur, which are expected to expand duty-free access from third countries and add further competitive pressure to an already strained domestic industry.
E42026-0032.name: Sugar Annual

E42026-0076.highlights: EU sugar production in MY 2026/27 is forecast to fall sharply, as a record-low planted area and a severe summer drought deliver the smallest EU crop since the end of the quota regime. Exports are expected to fall by more than half, while imports increase and stocks are drawn down to help cover the production shortfall. Consumption remains broadly stable, although a gradual structural decline continues. The Inward Processing (IP) regime, which allows duty-free imports of sugar for processing in the EU when the resulting products are re-exported, was suspended for raw cane sugar refining in May 2026 for one year, removing an important source of sugar imports for the EU market. EU prices, which fell steadily through the first half of 2026, are expected to firm as contracts for the new marketing year are negotiated against tighter supply and higher world prices.

Egyptian cotton imports are forecast at 1.2 million bales in MY 2026/27, up from an estimated 1.1 million bales in MY 2025/26, reflecting expansion of spinning capacity, supported by international investments in the Egyptian textile industry, low labor and energy costs, and Egypt's trade agreements. Brazil remains the most price-competitive supplier, while U.S. cotton is respected for quality but challenged by price and transit time. IN2026-0024.highlights: India's sugar sector is poised for recovery in marketing year 2026/27 following multiple years of production deficits. For the first time in two years, domestic production is expected to exceed consumption, marking a significant shift in supply dynamics. India's sugar consumption continues evolving along income-stratified patterns, with commercial and institutional buyers now dominating demand while affluent urban households increasingly shift toward alternative healthy sweeteners. Although total sugar imports are expected to remain steady for MY 2026/27, the expected recovery in production should provide India greater flexibility to meet domestic needs, fulfill international trade obligations, and support its ambitious ethanol blending targets.

IN2026-0026.highlights: FAS Mumbai forecasts India’s MY 2026/27 coffee production (Oct/Sep) at 6.14 million 60-kilgoram (kg) bags. Yields, particularly for Arabica, are expected to come under pressure due to excessive rainfall in January and February followed by an extended dry spell during the critical flowering and fruiting stage. Farmgate prices for Arabica and Robusta have declined by 16 percent and 11 percent respectively since October. Despite this change, prices remain at a premium to other origins, though further moderation is expected. The decline in prices is being driven by expectations of higher output in key producing countries and elevated domestic stock levels. Domestic consumption is projected to rise to 1.58 million 60-kg bags, supported by strong demand for soluble coffee. Exports are forecast to increase to 6.2 million 60-kg bags, supported by a higher exportable surplus and the recent implementation of free trade agreements, which are expected to enhance value-added coffee exports.
IN2026-0026.name: Coffee Annual

IN2026-0045.highlights: FAS Mumbai forecasts MY 2026/27 India cotton production at 24.5 million 480 lb. bales from 11.5 million hectares. Yields are forecast two percent lower at 464 kg per hectare due to forecasts for below-normal rainfall through August–September, with western and central India at greatest risk of extended dry spells. Although the cumulative monsoon deficit narrowed to 12 percent below normal by August 12, planting remains two percent behind last year, while reservoir storage is at 60 percent of capacity. Post raises its domestic mill use forecast to 26.2 million 480 lb. bales, driven by textile and apparel export orders. Higher minimum support prices and tighter crop prospects are expected to support firm lint prices, prompting mills to bridge fiber shortages through higher imports using duty-free export mechanisms if the general tariff exemption expires after October 31. As a result, raw cotton exportable surplus will remain constrained as available fiber is directed toward higher-value downstream manufacturing.
IN2026-0045.name: Cotton and Products Update

IN2026-0051.highlights: India sugar production for marketing year 2026/27 is forecast to drop as erratic rainfall, waterlogging, and pest infestation reduce cane yields and recovery rates, widening the gap between domestic consumption and production. Sharp price increases—the steepest in 25 years—have prompted duty-free raw sugar imports, inventory caps on bulk buyers, and an export ban to protect domestic supply.  Ending stocks for 2026/27 are forecast to decline sharply, reflecting weaker production, a thinner opening balance, and the continued suspension of imports, even as current-year stocks rise on the strength of expanded import allowances.

IV2026-0005.highlights: FAS Abidjan, Accra (Post) forecasts Côte d’Ivoire’s market year (MY) 2026/2027 (August-July) cotton fiber production at 590,000 bales (480 pounds -lb.), up by 25,000 bales or almost 4.5 percent, from the MY 2025/2026 estimate of 565,000 bales. Côte d’Ivoire’s cotton sector is in recovery, following an earlier cotton jassid infestation induced production drops. Previously, in MY 2024/2025, Côte d’Ivoire’s cotton fiber production had reached 613,000 bales. Post anticipates Ivorian cotton fiber exports following a similar recovery trend in MY 2026/2027, with exports of 610,000 bales, going up nearly 10 percent from the MY 2025/2026 estimate of  555,000 bales.
